Update to Fire TV Measurement Methodology : On October 8, 2026, Fire TV is updating its measurement methodology. Reported totals will no longer include impressions and clicks that do not align with the updated measurement criteria. Across Fire TV display supply, this update impacts approximately 15% of impressions and 11% of clicks. Individual advertiser impact will vary based on campaign, marketplace, and placement mix. All Fire TV impression forecasts have been updated, and reporting will follow the updated methodology. This update is aligned with MRC standards.

On this page Country-specific restrictions
Learn about Amazon Ads prohibited products and services to ensure that your ads align with global and regional compliance standards.
This section covers requirements for all ads. Additional country-specific and supply-specific restrictions may apply.
The following products and services are prohibited globally:
Products or services that facilitate deceptive or dishonest behavior
Products or services that cause damage, harm, or injury
Counterfeit or intellectual property infringing products
Inaccurate statements about prices, promotions, or discounts.
Political ads such as campaigns for or against a politician or a political party, content related to an election, active legislation, or content related to political issues of robust public debate.
Religious services, fundraising, proselytizing, or discriminatory religious content. This excludes religious books and merchandise.
Adult sexual products and services, such as:
Sexual enhancement, sexualized adult costumes, fetish and bondage wear, novelty underwear, sex toys, sexually graphic novelty items, sex games, sex furniture, sexually explicit underwear/clothing, and other similar items. Review Healthcare products and services policy for allowed sexual wellness products.
Sexual services such as escorts, prostitution, strip clubs, phone sex lines, pornography, or other similar services
Products or services that facilitate human trafficking or sexual exploitation.
Recreational drugs and all related products and services, including paraphernalia, masking products, nitrous oxide, storage devices, and products and services that make claims to 'cure' addiction.
Products and services designed exclusively for use by military, law enforcement, or medical professionals.
All tobacco and nicotine products, including e-cigarettes, nicotine pouches, heat-not-burn products, shisha/hookah, and related accessories.
Weapons, including parts or accessories, such as:
Guns, knives, and associated accessories (some knives are permitted, review Outdoor recreational weapons ).
Products to conceal weapons products.
Products resembling realistic weapons.
Instructional guides on how to use or how to build weapons.
Permanent tattoo products and devices that puncture the skin, leave a permanent scar or marking, and/or apply pigment under the skin.
Products that contain or imply that they contain THC, CBD, or full spectrum hemp. This excludes hemp products without THC or CBD.
Imagery associated with recreational drugs or psychoactive effects.
Premium pay-per-call services.
Products that harm animals or contain parts or ingredients from endangered or threatened animals.
News and journalism (excludes books and merchandise).
Specific kinds of food where advertising of such products is prohibited by local law. For example, pork products.
Infant formula, where it's prohibited by law. Review Baby formula and feeding accessories policy for regional guidelines.
